conventions.units: SVG root width/height are inches; viewBox is 0.01 in per user unit; anchors/landmarks are in user units, origin top-left of the artwork box.
conventions.layers: A layer (nametag, board, braid, epaulet sleeve) shares its base garment box and registers at 0,0; draw order is base garment, then layers, then insignia at the layer slots.
conventions.hats: A hat or cap asset is placed by aligning its garment_attach_center with the garment top_center (cap sits on the top edge of the artwork box).
conventions.cords: A shoulder cord is placed by its shoulder_seam_attach on the garment epaulet strap axis (centred, 0.125 in toward the neck), under the epaulet sleeve.
conventions.epaulet_sleeves: Use the garment-*-epaulet-sleeve-* layers for sleeve shape on the shirts and put grade insignia at rank_slot; rank-epaulet-sleeve-* are standalone graded sleeves (1.97 x 3.84 in) and are wider than the drawn strap.
conventions.size_source: regulation = dimension from a regulation or purchase description; measured = measured from a reference at a stated scale; estimated = assumed (see basis).

LIVE9-ART 2: drawn as worn on a USAF service dress coat (assets/cords/ref/aiguillette-worn-usaf-service-dress-screenshot.jpg, README), in braid thicknesses B (0.30 in here): two braids leaving the epaulet at the top (cut square here: the ends go under it) side by side, 0.9 B apart: the inner one makes a short loop (legs 2.24 B apart, bottom 10.0 B below the epaulet edge), the outer one a long loop (legs 4.14 B apart, bottom 15.2 B as photographed), each turning up on the chest side into a free end 3.9 B below the epaulet edge; from each free end a thin cord (0.14 B) runs to a whipping (0.7 x 1.8 B at 6.7 B) and on to a silver pencil tip 3.2 B long (0.96 in at B 0.30), the two tips 0.8 B apart ending 14.7 B below the epaulet edge. There is no separate run along the shoulder. B was read on the photo (about 50 px at x4 of the 314 x 236 px preview); every depth and width is read in B from the same picture. How the loops hang is as photographed, a mannequin.

Outline traced from images/base/ABU_male.webp (581x719 px) at 0.0474 in/px, chosen so the coat is 29.96 in long. No real garment was measured. Body basis only: MIL-DTL-44048H (BDU-style combat coat) gives the same body (Medium Regular half chest 24-1/4 in, back length about 29-3/8 to 29-1/2 in, Large about 30 in), so the 29.96 in length is consistent with a Large Regular; that spec has no pocket sizes in its text, so pocket, tape and button sizes remain estimates. Sleeve cap/width widened by script (same as the OCP coat). Print cell: 1/16 in, from the weave pitch of the cloth (abu-weave-measure.json) and the autocorrelation of the Vanguard coat front (abu-scale-check.json), not from the tape or the pocket size (the pockets and tape are estimates).

Silhouette traced from images/base/aviator_shirt_female.webp (581x719 px; the female outline is traced from the clean 1130x1392 re-render of the same drawing) at 0.0376 in per 581-px-canvas px, chosen so the shirt is the same body width as the Class B shirt (20.8 in sleeve to sleeve before the sleeves were widened). The two sleeves are then widened outward by up to 0 in (smooth ramp from the shoulder end at 5.06 in to full at 9.63 in below the top, body side untouched) so the regulation 3 1/2 in chevron sits on the sleeve: the hanging view traced here is only 3.5 in wide at the chevron line (x 1.204 after the scale). The widening is an estimate (the regulation gives no sleeve width). Then the whole sheet is scaled by 1.2037 (LIVE-ART2 item 1; 0.0376 in/px becomes 0.0453): the men's pocket measures 4.36 in wide on the traced image and a USAF-style men's size-M short-sleeve shirt pocket is about 5.25 x 6 in (ESTIMATE: AF shirt pattern dimension supplied with the task; no CAPR 39-1 or DAFI 36-2903 dimension), so the men's pocket is drawn 5.25 x 6.0 in and the women's shirt, registered to the men's, takes the same scale (its traced pocket becomes about 5.5 in wide). Nametag and ribbon slots, edge-on strip thickness and the tie tab keep their true size. No real garment was measured.

Two bands lying along the FDU collar V and crossing where they are tucked in; sized to the suit's collar opening. CAPR 39-1 8.2.6 / Figure 8.2 give no dimensions. Motif is an original simplified three-pronged mark, not traced.

Shape follows CAPR 39-1 Figure 8.1. The whole figure is scaled so that its front zipper (591 px at 25.55 px/in = 23.13 in) equals the 28 in front-opening slide fastener of a 40R coverall: scale factor 1.210. This is ONE linear constraint, not a pattern measurement: the spec has no finished body table, and the figure is stylised (its pockets are larger than the spec zipper lengths imply, so pocket zippers are drawn at 6.5 in and 4.75 in and the pocket panels are estimates). Nominal size 40R, chosen to match the MA-1 jacket Medium. The suit is a top only, cut about 37.5 in below the collar tips.

Outline traced from images/base/ABU_male.webp (581x719 px) at 0.0474 in/px, chosen so the coat is 29.96 in long. No real garment was measured. Body basis only: MIL-DTL-44048H (BDU-style combat coat) gives the same body (Medium Regular half chest 24-1/4 in, back length about 29-3/8 to 29-1/2 in, Large about 30 in), so the 29.96 in length is consistent with a Large Regular; that spec has no pocket sizes in its text, so pocket, tape and button sizes remain estimates. Sleeve cap/width widened by script (same as the OCP coat).

Heights, shoulders, collar, V, lapels, front edge, buttons, flaps' inner ends, front seams and hem measured on Vanguard's photo of the CAP women's blue blazer CAP4200E on a form (base-art/bz_photo.png, mask bz_alpha.png), both halves averaged and drawn as clean geometry (LIVE12-ART 10). Scale: the shoulders, 310 px outline corner to outline corner, are 15.97 in (the women's 12R of the Class A fit): 0.05152 in/px; the photo's buttons then measure 0.75 in, the 30-ligne blazer button. The photo's half-widths are a frontal projection of a garment hanging on a form (sleeve to sleeve 19.06 in, torso 11.5 in at the hem, 1.5 in of breast between the lapel edge and the hanging sleeve's front edge), so the torso sides, the armhole seam and the sleeves are drawn in the regulation figures' convention (LIVE13-ART 19, E123): the armhole seam is the men's sheet's (Fig 4.14) scaled by the shoulder points, 7.99 / 10.10, from the shoulder point to 6.77 in out at 15.05 in down, the torso straight below it (13.54 in wide at the hem; a women's 12R has a men's 40R's 40 in chest on 15.97 in shoulders); the sleeves bulge Fig 4.15's 2.58 in beyond the shoulder point (10.56 in out, 21.13 in across) and end 2.83 in across (Fig 4.15). Blazer 28.28 in from collar top to hem (the photo; Fig 4.15 draws 24.79, a 12R blazer is 26 to 27 in from the shoulder seam). The tie tab is the Fig 4.11 tab (tie.js). Chest: the nametag, crest and medal slot sit on the body between the lapel edge and the armhole seam, 1/4 in clear of both, at the first height from the pocket top (9.50 in, the photo's welt) down where all three fit: tag top 10.85 in, crest centre (5.25, 13.65) in (4.2.4.1.1.1, 4.2.4.1.1.2, 4.2.2.4; see placement).

Silhouette traced from images/base/male_semi_formal.webp (581x719 px) at 0.0474 in/px, which makes the sleeve-to-sleeve 25.12 in (a men's 40R; the Class A coat at its true scale, make-blues-a.js, is 25.27 in). Trousers are added below the base image's cropped hem. No real garment was measured. Checked against CAPR 39-1 Fig 4.14 (PDF page 87 at 8x) with the figure's 1398 px sleeve-to-sleeve taken as the sheet's 25.12 in (55.6 px/in): the figure's crest centre is 5.53 in from the centre line (Fig 4.12, page 84: 5.37 in), the sheet's pocket and crest centre are 5.49 in from it; the sheet's silhouette, pocket top (12.38 in), crest and lapel overlaid on Fig 4.14 agree within 0.1 in. The lapel is the figure's: its peak is 5.58 in from the centre line at y 6.1 in, the lapel 3.9 in wide, its outer edge 5.35 / 4.44 / 3.97 / 2.84 in from the centre line at y 7.3 / 9.4 / 10.4 / 12.4 in. A rack of 4 miniatures at 11/16 in (2.75 in wide) centred on the pocket has its inner edge 4.12 in from the centre line, so the lapel edge crosses its top rows (1.23 in over the rack at y 7.3, 0.32 in at y 9.4) and clears it from y 10.4 down; Fig 4.12 draws the rack the same way, its top rows against the lapel edge. Moving the pocket out or narrowing the lapel enough to clear the top rows would leave Figs 4.12 and 4.14 (see DECISIONS.md DORAN5-ART-2).

Outline traced from images/base/ABU_male.webp (581x719 px) at 0.0474 in/px, chosen so the coat is 29.96 in long. No real garment was measured. CAPR 39-1 Fig A5-1 / A5-6 give no inch size. Scale 178 px per inch from the 1 in oak leaf on the Major sleeve in Fig A5-1; trapezoid (350 px bottom, 306 px top, 684 px tall at that scale) and all feature positions measured on the figure. Officer sleeves come in two sizes (standard / smaller); the figure shows no measurable difference, so one size is built. Same box as the garment sheet; colours from assets/cords/cord-aide-de-camp.spec.json. The regulation gives no cord dimension. LIVE11-ART 1 (Ethan: "theres only supposed to be one thing not 2"): the aide de camp cord is ONE aiguillette, drawn as worn on a USAF service dress coat (assets/cords/ref/aiguillette-worn-usaf-service-dress-screenshot.jpg, README), in braid thicknesses B (0.36 in): two braids leave the epaulet at the front of the shoulder side by side, 0.9 B apart; the outer one is the group `cord`, the run down the armhole seam to the armpit that the engine fits and carries under the arm along the body edge, and it is the right leg of the long loop; the inner one makes the short loop (legs 2.24 B apart, bottom 10.0 B below the epaulet edge); the long loop's chest-side leg hangs 4.14 B from the run, parallel to it, and bends in to meet the run under the arm (where the engine fades the braid out behind the arm); each loop turns up on the chest side into a free end 3.9 B below the epaulet edge, from which a thin cord (0.14 B) runs to a whipping (0.7 x 1.8 B) and on to a silver pencil tip 3.2 B long (1.15 in), the two tips 0.8 B apart, ending 14.7 B below the epaulet edge. There is no separate braid along the seam: the run is the aiguillette. B is the braid thickness read on the photo (about 50 px at x4 of the 314 x 236 px preview); the leg offsets, loop depths and widths are read in B from the same picture; the long loop's depth to the armpit and the under-arm closing are not in the photo (it is cropped there) and are estimated from the sheet's armpit and body edge. The drape is measured along the run (its legs follow the armhole seam), the free ends and tips hang parallel to it. How the real cord hangs on a person varies; the photograph is one mannequin.

Diameter 1.25 in, estimated: neither CAPR 39-1, ICL 25-02 nor the Vanguard product page ("Civil Air Patrol Cap Device: NCO Cap Device", SKU CAP0748R) prints a size. The listed shipping weight, 18 g, equals the officer flight cap device (SKU CAP0748OA, 18 g), which Vanguard prints at 1 1/4 x 1 1/4 in, so the NCO device is drawn 1.25 in across. It is round: the outer ring of the listing photo fits a true circle (radius 294.6 px, residual within 5 px), so height = width (the photo frame is 600 x 623 px only because of its white margins)

Measured on the sleeve of the sheet garment-aviator-shirt-female-long (long sleeve: the traced short sleeve and its extension to the wrist; widened as dimensions.sleeve_widening; sheet scale k 1.2037): the sleeve is the strip between the sheet's outline and its armhole seam (below the seam, between the outline and the arm/body gap); stations run along the outer edge and widths are taken square to the sleeve's axis (the axis leans 0.70 deg on the sheet), smoothed over 1.6 in before the pi / 2 (the traced edges are polylines, and the inner edge changes from the armhole seam to the arm/body gap part-way down). Length, shoulder seam to cuff along the outer edge: 29.49 in (the straight axis is 29.00 in). Width: the sheet draws the sleeve hanging, so the width it shows is the sleeve's diameter (circumference / pi); laid flat the sleeve is circumference / 2 wide, so every hanging width is multiplied by pi / 2 = 1.571. Hanging widths on the sheet: 4.47 in at its widest, 3.99 in at the elbow, 2.61 in at the cuff (0.4 in above the lower edge); flat widths: 7.02 in at its widest (the cap width, the width below the shoulder seam), 6.27 in at the elbow, 4.11 in at the cuff, i.e. 14.03 in around at the widest and 8.21 in around at the cuff (a real men's shirt sleeve is roughly 15 to 17 in around at the bicep and a short sleeve hem 14 to 16 in around: the sheet's sleeve was widened so the chevron fits, see its sleeve_widening). The flat opens to its widest width over a rounded cap (a half ellipse 0.45 x that width deep) and keeps at least that width until the measured profile narrows. Chevron: CAPR 39-1 4.2.6.2.3: "NCOs will wear 3 ½ inch chevron grade centered on the outer arm halfway between the shoulder seam and elbow when bent at a 90-degree angle (long sleeved-shirt) or bottom edge of the sleeve (short sleeved-shirt)", so chevron_center is on the centre line 8.11 in below the shoulder seam (halfway to the elbow, which is taken at 55 % of the length as on the sheet, an anatomical estimate). ESTIMATED: the sheet's sleeve is a hanging front view that was widened so the 3 1/2 in chevron fits (its sleeve_widening, an estimate), and the regulation gives no sleeve dimension; the cuff band and button are schematic.

Measured on photographs of real CAP polo shirts and CAP's own drawing, no longer traced from CAPR 39-1 Figure 5.5 (Ethan: "it just.... doesn't look right. look at some pictures of seniors wearing the polo"): a small flat knit collar (points 4.2 in below the collar's top, 7.3 in tip to tip; Figure 5.5's long dress-shirt points were 11.2 in apart), a short placket (5.9 in, 3 buttons) and a shorter sleeve (8.9 in along its outer edge, was 10.6). Sources (screenshots kept in base-art/polo-ref/ with a README; measure.js repeats the pixel readings): ref4 = a knit CAP seal polo with pocket on a ghost mannequin (Edwards label; the best-resolved photo, shirt 490 px wide); ref3 = Vanguard CAP0694A, navy knit polo with pocket and a white seal; ref2 = CAP's wing page photo set of the Corporate Working Uniform shirts (https://ftsnelling.cap.gov/media/cms/_Corporate_Working_header_9930F3D215143.jpg); ref1 = CAP's own uniform-guidance drawing (https://falcon305.cap.gov/media/cms/polo_3D9EF39C1FEBB.png). SCALE (ESTIMATE; the regulation gives no garment dimension): the embroidered seal is the ruler for every local feature, 66 x 68 px on ref4 = 2.93 in (the seal slot, unchanged), K = 0.0444 in/px; body-level horizontal distances (shoulder, sleeve, side seam) keep the wearer's pit-to-pit width of the earlier sheets, 2 x 7.721 in (the Class B shirt's same-wearer width), because the ref4 mannequin is a slim 301 px = 13.4 in across at the seal ruler (stretch 0.0513 / 0.0444 = 1.16). The guidance drawing read at its own seal (20 px = 2.93 in) is 102 px = 14.9 in pit to pit, within 3 % of the sheet's 15.44 in. Measured on ref4 (K, px to in): the collar (widths at the body-level scale, because the neck sits inside the shoulders; heights at the seal ruler): the back arch is 75 px (3.85 in) wide at its top and the points hang 94 px (4.2 in) below the arch's top (the leaf's outer edge 56 px = 2.5 in), 143 px (7.3 in) tip to tip, the leaf's inner-bottom corners 47 px (2.4 in) apart, the neck opening 97 px (5.0 in) wide at row 60; the placket 29 px wide (385 to 414, 1.29 in) and 132 px long (5.9 in) with buttons 42 px (1.9 in) apart at rows 142 and 184 (the top button sits under the leaves); the pocket 94 px wide (4.17 in), 90 px (4.0 in) to the end of its sides and 109.5 px (4.9 in) to its point, its top hem with two stitch lines 11.5 and 20 px (0.5 and 0.9 in) below the top; the seal's centre 0.51 in below the pocket's top and 4.34 in right of the centre line (the pocket's centre 4.46 in the other way; positions use the body-level scale); the shoulder point 4.5 in below the collar's top, the sleeve's outer edge 8.9 in long to the hem's outer corner (the shoulder point to the corner is 8.2 in down), its hem edge slanting down 1.6 in to the armpit, the armpit 14.4 in below the collar's top. Body = the p30-p70 mean, lit tone = the p85-p97 mean (stitch and fold lines only), shadow / outline = the p0-p10 mean. Sources (screenshots kept in base-art/polo-ref/ with a README; measure.js repeats the pixel readings): ref4 = a knit CAP seal polo with pocket on a ghost mannequin (Edwards label; the best-resolved photo, shirt 490 px wide); ref3 = Vanguard CAP0694A, navy knit polo with pocket and a white seal; ref2 = CAP's wing page photo set of the Corporate Working Uniform shirts (https://ftsnelling.cap.gov/media/cms/_Corporate_Working_header_9930F3D215143.jpg); ref1 = CAP's own uniform-guidance drawing (https://falcon305.cap.gov/media/cms/polo_3D9EF39C1FEBB.png). SCALE (ESTIMATE; the regulation gives no garment dimension): the women's collar, placket and button column are the men's measurements (ref4, seal ruler K = 0.0444 in/px = the 2.93 in seal) scaled by 0.93 (the women's neck is smaller; no women's photograph is large enough to measure: ref2's women's knit is 80 px pit to pit); the shoulder line, the sleeve's outer edge and the torso below the armpit are the women's figure of CAPR 39-1 Figure 5.5 (0.03495 in/px from the seal, 94.9 px = 2.93 in on the men's figure, 83.9 px here), the same drawing as the guidance drawing ref1, whose women's pit (74 px), waist (65) and hem (97) give the same flare; the sleeve is shortened to the men's proportion (its outer edge ends 12.35 in below the collar's top, was 13.9) and its hem takes the men's measured hem curve. The women's polo is worn out over the skirt (5.3.1): the hem is straight, below the hip. Long sleeves: the arm below the short sleeve's end follows the Class B long-sleeve sheet's arm (class_b_female_long_outline.json, K-scaled) shifted to the polo's sleeve width; ESTIMATE. Everything below the armpit (the tucked body to the belt, belt, loops, buckle and trousers; the women's torso and skirt) is still read off Figure 5.5 (base-art/ref_polo_CAPR_fig5-5.png, PDF page 108 at 300 dpi, trace-polo.js; men 0.0309 in/px from the 64 px buckle = the 2 in limit of 5.3.5, women 0.03495 in/px).
